# =============================================================================
# FLOP PROTOCOL PARAMETERS — CANONICAL SOURCE OF TRUTH
# =============================================================================
#
# This file is the single source of truth for FLOP's *protocol* parameters
# (emission, staking, subsidy, agent limits, consensus timing). Implementations
# in Rust (runtime + consensus), the TypeScript SDK, and the simulator MUST
# match the values here.
#
# Propagation is ENFORCED by `scripts/check_params.py` in the authoring
# repository (run in CI and via the lefthook pre-commit hook): for every
# `enforced` parameter, each listed implementation site must contain the
# `expect` snippet. The implementation files are not part of the public mirror,
# so there the script reports them missing. If you change a value:
#   1. edit `value` here,
#   2. update each implementation's `expect` snippet AND the code it points to,
#   3. run `uv run --script scripts/check_params.py` until green.
#
# Scope: PROTOCOL parameters only. The simulator's *modeling* parameters (Bass
# diffusion, feedback-loop coefficients, microsim distributions) remain in
# `ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml`; that file's protocol values are kept in sync
# via the enforcement below. See `docs/PARAMETERS.md` for the full model.
#
# Relationship to the yellowpaper: the yellowpaper is the narrative/economic
# spec; THIS file is the machine-checkable numeric contract derived from it.
#
# Deployment contract (including reference entries): `on_chain.constants` names
# FRAME metadata constants (api.consts), and `on_chain.storage` names effective
# scalar storage (api.query). `source_only` is an explicit reason for no RPC check,
# not permission to silently ignore an absent mapped constant. FLOP amounts use
# meta.decimals; multiplier/divisor handle Perbill and per-byte encodings.
# `mutability` describes the shipped value: runtime-upgrade-only means new WASM
# (system.setCode), governance-settable names a wired Root setter, genesis-only
# describes initial allocations, and source-only means no deployed setting exists.
# For governed storage, changing its compiled default still requires an upgrade
# (`default_mutability`); a storage setter only changes the effective override.
# `on_chain.pending_upgrade: {runtime: <spec_version>, reason: "..."}` marks a
# canonical value the deployed chain does not carry yet. Its drift prints PENDING
# only while the deployed spec_version is below `runtime`; at or above it, drift fails
# and so does the marker. A marker whose sites all match also fails (stale).
# `on_chain.governed_value` + `governed_by: "<setter call, referendum or tx, date>"`
# (governance-settable only) record the effective storage value after a setter call;
# storage sites compare against it, compiled constants still compare to `value`.
# The calibration 64/600 constants have NO governance setter. Devnet realignment
# was assigned to the HEAD-runtime regenesis (#1592), not a separate setCode.
# Check a finalized deployed block with:
#   uv run --script scripts/check_deployed_params.py --rpc-url http://devnet.ts.flop.network
# =============================================================================

meta:
  version: 1
  decimals: 18              # 1 FLOP = 10^18 base units
  block_time_seconds: 1
  blocks_per_day: 86_400
  halving_interval_days: 730

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ENFORCED PARAMETERS — verified against implementations by check_params.py.
# Each `expect` is a literal substring that must be present in `file`.
# `count` (optional) requires that many occurrences.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
parameters:

  # ---- Genesis ----
  - name: genesis_supply
    mutability: genesis-only
    on_chain: {source_only: Not exported as a FRAME constant; verified against source only.}
    value: 4_400_000_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0440
    rust: FLOP_TOTAL_SUPPLY
    lean: HalvingBoundary.genesisSupply
    quint: GENESIS_MICRO
    description: >
      Genesis (pre-emission) total supply, pinned normatively by R9.7 (§9.3). Components (D-0440,
      tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010 sec. 2.1): miner airdrop 1,200,000,000 + validator airdrop 1,200,000,000 +
      agent airdrop 1,200,000,000 + ecosystem reserve 800,000,000 = exactly 4,400,000,000. Each
      component is pinned by its own enforced param below, so the four cannot drift apart from
      this total. There are no genesis auctions, and Team is NOT genesis-allocated — Labs and
      Foundation receive a per-block subsidy instead (D-0421). D-0440 resized the pool 3,500,000,000
      → 4,400,000,000 to absorb the validator bond raise (validator_min_stake 305,505 → 1,200,000):
      the bond IS the validator cohort, so at the old pool the four components summed to
      3,600,000,000 and the residual reserve went NEGATIVE. Allocation history is in
      whitepaper/decisions/v0.4.md (D-0421, D-0435, D-0438, D-0440).
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "total: 4400000000" }
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/genesis_config_presets/helper.rs, expect: "FLOP_TOTAL_SUPPLY: Balance = 4_400_000_000 * VFY" }
      - { file: README.md, expect: "4,400,000,000 FLOP" }   # narrative: Key Parameters table
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Genesis.lean, expect: "def genesisSupply : ℕ := 4400000000 * baseUnit" }  # FG-20: Lean const bound to source-of-truth

  - name: genesis_miner_airdrop
    mutability: genesis-only
    on_chain: {source_only: 'Model, SDK, or documented value; no exported on-chain constant.'}
    value: 1_200_000_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0438
    description: >
      Miner-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). One of the three D-0421 airdrops, as
      re-balanced by D-0435 and re-scaled by D-0438 (ECON-009 sec. 2.1). D-0440 held the absolute
      grant at 1,200,000,000 while resizing the pool, so only its share moved 34.29% → 27.27%
      (ECON-010 sec. 2.1). Home: §9.3. The workbook
      presents it as
      testnet block reward 559,872,000 + capped testnet fee pool 640,128,000; the fee cap is
      back-solved so the pool lands on exactly 1,200,000,000, so treat the round pool as the
      ratified quantity, not as an output of the testnet model. This is the actual testnet→mainnet
      conversion pool (assignPool in testnet-conversion.ts), so it must not silently diverge from
      the split; the total (genesis_supply) is enforced above, this pins the component too.
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "minerAirdrop: 1_200_000_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "miner_airdrop: 1200000000" }

  - name: genesis_validator_airdrop
    mutability: genesis-only
    on_chain: {source_only: 'Model, SDK, or documented value; no exported on-chain constant.'}
    value: 1_200_000_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0440
    description: >
      Validator-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). Home: §9.3. D-0435 (tokenomics
      workbook rev 2026-08-20; ECON-008 sec. 2.3) cut the validator grant to the bond and nothing else:
      the aggregate bond, granted free and bonded at launch, with no airdrop beyond it. That
      identity is unchanged — the grant IS validator_min_stake × validator_active_set_cap — so
      D-0440's bond raise 305,505 → 1,200,000 carries the cohort 305,505,000 → 1,200,000,000
      (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010 sec. 2.1). This is what forced the pool resize:
      at the old 3,500,000,000 the four components summed to 3,600,000,000 and genesis_reserve, the
      residual leg, went to MINUS 100,000,000. Consumed directly as a conversion pool by assignPool
      in testnet-conversion.ts (per-cohort pools, not one miner pool), so it is pinned here too:
      otherwise the validator pool could drift from the ratified split while check_params.py still
      passed. This CLOSES ECON-009 gap G2 (issue #1353): the bonded stake is the only slashing
      collateral in the system, and it now grows with the float instead of falling behind it —
      12.30% → 8.73% under D-0438, back to 27.27% here.
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "validatorAirdrop: 1_200_000_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "validator_airdrop: 1200000000" }

  - name: genesis_agent_airdrop
    mutability: genesis-only
    on_chain: {source_only: 'Model, SDK, or documented value; no exported on-chain constant.'}
    value: 1_200_000_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0438
    description: >
      Agent-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). Home: §9.3. D-0440 held the absolute
      grant at 1,200,000,000 while resizing the pool, so only its share moved 34.29% → 27.27%
      (ECON-010 sec. 2.1); gap G1 below is unaffected, the pool size being unchanged. D-0438 (tokenomics
      workbook rev 2026-08-22; ECON-009 sec. 2.1) doubled it from the 596,030,400 that ECON-007
      sec. 3.5 adopted, to a
      round 1,200,000,000, historically sized as an agent spend cap of 600,000,000 plus a testnet
      prize pool of 600,000,000 (D-0438 sizing rationale, not the current grant split). Consumed
      directly as a conversion pool by assignPool in testnet-conversion.ts, so it is pinned here
      alongside the miner and validator components. Its grants unlock by spend-to-unlock (yellowpaper
      §8.2 R8.7, D-0522): one FLOP per three FLOP of locked principal spent in settled sessions, spend capped at
      three quarters of principal, no end block. All Era-0 allocations land as grants (R8.6); across
      this pool D-0522 caps locked spend at 900,000,000 and unlocked principal at 300,000,000.
      With no end block, ECON-009 gap G1's demand shortfall
      slows the unlock rather than breaking a schedule; no code reads spend_to_unlock.agent_ratio_n
      today (#1354).
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "agentAirdrop: 1_200_000_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "agent_airdrop: 1200000000" }

  - name: genesis_reserve
    mutability: genesis-only
    on_chain: {source_only: 'Model, SDK, or documented value; no exported on-chain constant.'}
    value: 800_000_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0440
    description: >
      Ecosystem/incentives reserve component of the genesis supply (18.18%) — KOL, referral and
      growth incentives. Home: §9.3. NOT an airdrop, so D-0421's "three airdrops only" stays
      intact. Promoted to an enforced param by D-0435 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-20;
      ECON-008 sec. 2.3): it
      previously existed only in the simulator, so nothing stopped the four genesis components
      from drifting away from genesis_supply. It is the residual leg — D-0438 fixed the miner,
      validator and agent cohorts and this absorbs the rest of the pool, as it absorbed what the
      D-0435 validator-grant cut freed. D-0440 fixed all three cohorts at 1,200,000,000 and sized
      the pool so this residual lands on a round 800,000,000 (was 794,495,000; ECON-010 sec. 2.1) —
      at the pre-resize 3,500,000,000 pool the same residual would have been MINUS 100,000,000.
      Release cadence per the workbook's Airdrop Schedule sec. 3 is 20% at Season 0 (160,000,000) then
      eight half-year seasons of 80,000,000 to +48mo; D-0438's four annual tranches of 158,899,000
      are superseded. Controller and release rules are still undefined
      (ECON-008 sec. 7 C7, ECON-009 gap G3) and it has no runtime presence yet.
      Under D-0531 (closing #1358), the workbook's legacy on-chain referral commission model (6–10%) is superseded by a public explorer leaderboard and periodic referral lotteries funded from this reserve and settled off-chain.
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "FLOP_GENESIS_RESERVE = 800_000_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "reserve_airdrop: 800000000" }

  - name: validator_min_stake
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {constants: [Validators.InitialMinimumStake]}
    effective_mutability: governance-settable (Validators.force_set_minimum_stake); effective stake also grows with time, so only the initial constant is diffed
    value: 1_200_000
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0440
    rust: ValidatorInitialMinimumStake
    description: >
      Baseline floor; compounds 9%/yr (MinimumValidatorStake). COUPLED to V_booked (realized effective value), NOT to reward — D-0413 (C5). Effective floor enforced at registration + committee admission = max(baseline, k·V_booked), ratcheted (never below baseline, composes with C6 thermostat). baseline = the CoCVoC required-stake requirement: ~1,163,309 FLOP at 96 FLOP/block (Lean Security.lean::CoCVoC.stake_at_current_params; the legacy 305,505 FAILS the deterrence margin — legacy_stake_insufficient_at_r96). THRESHOLD-ROBUST: in the reward-capture requiredStake the corruption fraction θ CANCELS, so 1/3 (the AlephBFT safety threshold, Consensus.quorum_inter_gt_third) vs the earlier '51%' framing barely moves the ~1.16M (51% is a Nakamoto number, not a BFT one). CAVEAT: this reward-pegged base FALLS with each halving (reward_floor_shrinks_across_halving) — it prices reward-capture, not value-at-risk; the DURABLE floor is the value-coupled k·V_booked below, not this baseline. RATIFIED AT 1,200,000 BY D-0440 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010): the superseded 305,505 predated both the 96-FLOP decision and the V_booked retarget, and Lean already proved it inadequate — legacy_stake_insufficient_at_r96 machine-checks that it FAILS the 1.22x margin at R=96, while scaled_stake_sufficient_at_r96 proves 1,200,000 HOLDS it. The shipped floor is now the value the spec proves sufficient, closing ECON-009 C1 / issue #1353. Because the aggregate bond IS the validator genesis cohort (genesis_validator_airdrop), this raise carried that cohort 305,505,000 -> 1,200,000,000 and forced the genesis_supply resize to 4,400,000,000. Runtime wiring LANDED (pallet_validators::ValueCoupledStakeFloor / effective_minimum_stake / set_value_coupled_floor, #86); k + retarget cadence calibration is governance/ENG-31. Stake-side coupling is non-inflationary.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/lib.rs, expect: "ValidatorInitialMinimumStake: Balance = 1_200_000 * VFY" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml, expect: "validator_min_stake: 1200000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "validatorMinStake: 1_200_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/julia/params_sensitivity.yaml, expect: "validator_min_stake: 1200000" }
      - { file: formal-specs/staking/staking-verification-minimal.qnt, expect: "STAKE_REQUIRED: int = 1200000" }

  - name: airdrop_vesting_duration_blocks
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {constants: [AirdropVesting.VestingDurationBlocks]}
    value: 7_776_000
    unit: blocks
    decision: SPEC-022
    description: >
      Interim pallet schedule: 90-day linear airdrop vesting at 1-second block time, governing no
      ratified grant tier (§8.2). The airdrop-vesting pallet
      applies it to every tier today; under yellowpaper §8.2 R8.7 (D-0517, D-0522, D-0527) no
      ratified grant tier uses this duration (Miner grants unlock against miner block rewards and
      settled sessions, Agent grants against settled sessions, both with no end block; Validator
      grants follow the first-halving freeze and daily release), so it is only the pallet's interim
      schedule until R8.7 is implemented.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/pallets/airdrop-vesting/src/lib.rs, expect: "VESTING_DURATION_BLOCKS: u32 = 7_776_000" }
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/lib.rs,        expect: "AirdropVestingDurationBlocks: u32 = 7_776_000" }
      - { file: pallets/pallets/airdrop-vesting/README.md,  expect: "VestingDurationBlocks = ConstU32<7_776_000>" }
      - { file: docs/tokenomics/SPEC-022-performance-vesting.md, expect: "| `VestingDurationBlocks` | **7,776,000** |" }

  # ---- Emission & Rewards ----
  - name: initial_block_reward
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {constants: [BlockRewards.InitialRewardPerBlock]}
    value: 96
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-008
    rust: RewardInitialPerBlock
    lean: Emission.initialReward
    quint: P_EMISSION_CAP
    description: Block reward at genesis (Era 0). Halves every halving interval.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/lib.rs,                       expect: "RewardInitialPerBlock: Balance = 96 * VFY" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts,               expect: "initialReward: 96," }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,                           expect: "initial_reward: 96" }
      # Narrative docs — drifted to the old 25 FLOP after D-008; enforced so they can't again.
      - { file: README.md,                                  expect: "Block Reward (Era 0) | 96 FLOP/block" }
      - { file: docs/plans/PROTOCOL_IMPLEMENTATION.md,       expect: "**Initial Block Reward** | 96 FLOP" }
      - { file: docs/plans/WHITEPAPER_IMPLEMENTATION.md,     expect: "INITIAL_REWARD = 96 FLOP" }
      - { file: docs/tokenomics/SPEC-018-halving-schedule.md, expect: "(spec: 96 FLOP)" }
      - { file: docs/tokenomics/TOKENOMICS_SPECIFICATION.md, expect: "**Initial Block Reward** | 96 FLOP/block" }
      # Governance anti-inflation bound = the genesis reward (no headroom cap); keep Quint + Lean aligned to 96 (#508).
      - { file: formal-specs/governance/governance.qnt,      expect: "P_EMISSION_CAP:    int = 96" }
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Governance.lean, expect: "p.emission ≤ 96" }

  - name: halving_interval_blocks
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {constants: [BlockRewards.HalvingIntervalBlocks]}
    value: 63_072_000
    unit: blocks
    description: Blocks between halvings (~730 days at 1s/block).
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/lib.rs,         expect: "RewardHalvingIntervalBlocks: u64 = 63_072_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "halvingIntervalBlocks: 63_072_000" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "halving_interval_blocks: 63072000" }

  - name: max_halvings
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {constants: [BlockRewards.MaxHalvings]}
    value: 5
    unit: count
    decision: D-0436
    rust: RewardMaxHalvings
    lean: Emission.maxHalvings
    quint: MAX_HALVINGS
    description: >
      Halvings before the reward floors permanently. Floor = initial >> max_halvings, so the
      ladder is 96 -> 48 -> 24 -> 12 -> 6 -> 3 and era 5 onward pays the 3 FLOP floor forever.
      D-0436 cut it from 6, superseding the sixth halving D-0421 added: the perpetual tail
      DOUBLES (floor_annual_emission 47,304,000 -> 94,608,000 FLOP/yr). This is a DELIBERATE,
      RECORDED DIVERGENCE from the tokenomics workbook (rev 2026-08-20, Tokenomics section 1),
      which still says "Number of halvings: 6" - see ECON-008 and D-0436.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/runtime/zkverify/src/lib.rs,         expect: "RewardMaxHalvings: u32 = 5" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "maxHalvings: 5" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "max_halvings: 5" }
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Tokenomics.lean, expect: "def maxHalvings : ℕ := 5" }

  - name: floor_reward
    mutability: source-only
    on_chain: {source_only: 'Model, SDK, or documented value; no exported on-chain constant.'}
    value: 3
    unit: FLOP
    decision: D-0436
    lean: Emission.floorReward
    quint: FLOOR_MICRO
    description: >
      Perpetual per-block reward after max_halvings (96 >> 5 = 3). DERIVED from
      initial_block_reward and max_halvings, never set independently. D-0436 raised it from 1.5
      by removing the sixth halving.
    implementations:
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "floorReward: 3" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "floor_reward: 3" }

  - name: miner_share_ppt
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {source_only: Not exported as a FRAME constant; verified against source only.}
    value: 750
    unit: parts-per-thousand
    decision: D-0435
    rust: MINER_SHARE_PPT
    lean: SettlementInt.BlockRewards.minerPpt
    description: >
      Miner share of each block reward (75%; yellowpaper §9). D-0435 (tokenomics workbook
      rev 2026-08-20;
      ECON-008 §2.1) cut it from 900 ppt: the miner leg is the RESIDUAL, and the new agent
      (100 ppt) and staker (50 ppt) legs are carved OUT of it, not added on top. The validator
      leg stays at 100 ppt, so YP §9.1 R9.5 ("the validator pool MUST NOT be increased") still
      holds. Supersedes D-0408's 90/10 split.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/pallets/block-rewards/src/lib.rs,    expect: "MINER_SHARE_PPT: u128 = 750" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "minerShare: 0.75" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "miner_share: 0.75" }
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Computable.lean, expect: "def minerPpt : Nat := 750" }   # proven money-path model + DRT oracle
      - { file: README.md,                                  expect: "75% Miners / 10% Validators / 10% Agents / 5% Stakers" }   # narrative: Key Parameters table

  - name: validator_share_ppt
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {source_only: Not exported as a FRAME constant; verified against source only.}
    value: 100
    unit: parts-per-thousand
    rust: VALIDATOR_SHARE_PPT
    lean: SettlementInt.BlockRewards.validatorPpt
    description: Validator share of each block reward (10%).
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/pallets/block-rewards/src/lib.rs,    expect: "VALIDATOR_SHARE_PPT: u128 = 100" }
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Computable.lean, expect: "def validatorPpt : Nat := 100" }   # proven money-path model + DRT oracle
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "validatorShare: 0.1" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "validator_share: 0.10" }

  - name: agent_share_ppt
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {source_only: Not exported as a FRAME constant; verified against source only.}
    value: 100
    unit: parts-per-thousand
    decision: D-0435
    rust: AGENT_SHARE_PPT
    lean: SettlementInt.BlockRewards.agentPpt
    description: >
      Agent/broker rebate share of each block reward (10%; yellowpaper §9). New in D-0435
      (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-20; ECON-008 §2.1, §3 F2) and carved OUT of the miner
      residual, not added on top — miner_share_ppt fell 900 → 750 to fund this leg and
      staker_share_ppt together. The
      DISTRIBUTION policy is not ratified: the pallet mints the leg to a sovereign PalletId
      account and emits an event, pending the F2 design decision. The macro simulator mints the
      leg every block and parks it in its own stock, outside circulating supply, mirroring the
      runtime.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/pallets/block-rewards/src/lib.rs,    expect: "AGENT_SHARE_PPT: u128 = 100" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/src/model/parameters.ts, expect: "agentShare: 0.1" }
      - { file: ai-agent-simulator/params.yaml,             expect: "agent_share: 0.10" }
      - { file: lean-proofs/FlopSpecs/Computable.lean, expect: "def agentPpt : Nat := 100" }   # proven money-path model + DRT oracle

  - name: staker_share_ppt
    mutability: runtime-upgrade-only
    on_chain: {source_only: Not exported as a FRAME constant; verified against source only.}
    value: 50
    unit: parts-per-thousand
    decision: D-0435
    rust: STAKER_SHARE_PPT
    lean: SettlementInt.BlockRewards.stakerPpt
    description: >
      Community-staker share of each block reward (5%; yellowpaper §9) — duration-locked community staking pool across seven lock duration tiers with zero slashing risk and no operator delegation (D-0530), for all FLOP stakers other than miners and validators. Decided 2026-08-04, ratified in D-0435 (tokenomics workbook
      rev 2026-08-20; ECON-008 §2.1, §3 F1) and carved OUT of the miner residual, not added on top. The
      DISTRIBUTION policy is not ratified: the pallet mints the leg to a sovereign PalletId
      account and emits an event, pending the F1 design decision. The macro simulator mints the
      leg every block and parks it in its own stock, outside circulating supply, mirroring the
      runtime.
    implementations:
      - { file: pallets/pallets/block-rewards/src/lib.rs,    expect: "STAKER_SHARE_PPT: u128 = 50" }
